analysis.title: Commodities Tracker October 2026
key_insights: Alphabet signed a 20-year agreement with Constellation Energy for 890 megawatts of new nuclear capacity on the PJM grid, an example of long-term corporate power contracts financing supply for data centres.

Italy's Senate backed legislation in September reopening the route to nuclear power after nearly four decades, with the government targeting nuclear generation by 2035. Timelines will determine when this becomes fuel demand.

Kazatomprom shareholders were reported in early October to have withheld approval for a proposed supply arrangement with Russia's Uranium One. The footnote source reports Kazatomprom rejected the Russian deal and approved supply to China.

The OECD NEA and IAEA 2026 Red Book warns of a possible uranium supply squeeze from the mid-2030s without timely mine investment, against a nuclear generating-capacity outlook at least 42% higher by 2050.
Chile copper output fell to its lowest since 2011 on severe weather, adding to concerns about a tightening physical market. Chile is the world's largest copper producer.
Codelco said it is investigating possible double-counting of copper output between divisions in earlier reporting periods. The findings are unresolved.
A key gauge of Chinese copper import demand reached a four-year high, suggesting possible consumer restocking in the world's largest copper market.
September reporting raised the possibility of a limited resumption of operations at Cobre Panamá to support an eventual orderly closure. A full restart would take time.
Copper inventories are unevenly distributed: elevated US stockpiles after inflows ahead of potential tariffs, low stockpiles in China. This has tightened metal availability outside the US.

Global gold ETFs took in a record US$31bn in Q3 2026, including US$10bn in September, led by European- and North American-listed funds. UK-listed funds had their strongest quarter on record and global ETF gold holdings reached a record 4,256 tonnes.
The People's Bank of China extended its reported gold buying streak to 23 consecutive months.

Interest-rate expectations are the dominant short-term driver for gold and silver. High energy costs are feeding inflation expectations, and stronger-than-expected US consumer prices spurred bets on more aggressive Federal Reserve tightening.
China's gold imports exceeded 1,000 tonnes in the first eight months of 2026, more than the full year of 2025.
Eramet plans a US$350 million lithium expansion in Argentina despite weaker lithium pricing.
China signalled willingness to facilitate rare earth and magnet export licensing to the EU, and the EU selected 46 projects to expand critical-materials supply.
Lynas Rare Earths proposed to acquire Meteoric Resources (US$672 million per the footnote source) as part of efforts to build ex-China supply.
BloombergNEF's Economic Transition Scenario projects lithium demand up 3.5-fold by 2040 versus 2025, copper 1.6x, cobalt 1.5x and nickel 1.4x. The Net Zero Scenario could be higher.

sector_views.rationale: Corporate power contracts, Italy's policy reversal and a projected supply gap from the mid-2030s support the long-term demand outlook.
Chilean output disruptions and stronger Chinese import demand point to possible physical tightness, with Cobre Panamá a supply variable.
Record ETF inflows, continued central bank buying and record Chinese imports show sustained investment demand, while rate expectations drive the short term.
Long-term demand projections encourage supply investment despite weaker near-term pricing, and policy is working to diversify processing away from China.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Cited in the footnote headline (FT, 14 October 2026) as driven by the Iran war. The body text says stronger-than-expected prices spurred bets on more Fed tightening, which weighs on gold and silver in the short term.

macro_indicators.reading: More than 1,000 tonnes in the first eight months of 2026
macro_indicators.interpretation: Exceeds the full year of 2025, indicating strong wealth-preservation demand.

macro_indicators.reading: US$31bn in Q3 2026, US$10bn in September
macro_indicators.interpretation: A record, showing sustained investor demand for bullion.
Underpins long-term uranium demand, with a supply squeeze possible from the mid-2030s.

risk_factors: Uranium mine development has long lead times and a supply shortfall is possible from the mid-2030s.
Cobre Panamá could return supply and ease copper tightness.
Further US tariff and trade policy shifts could disrupt copper flows.
Further Federal Reserve tightening could weigh on gold and silver.
Lithium project economics are sensitive to prices and funding conditions.
Lynas acquisition faces execution, permitting and processing capacity risks.
charts_described: Projected annual reactor-related uranium requirements to 2050, low and high projection, by region (axis up to 160,000 tU/y).
United States versus China copper inventories, March 2019 to September 2026, showing China Bonded, COMEX and SHFE.
China gold imports in USD billions, 2015 to 2026, described as a record this year.
BloombergNEF demand index (base 2025 = 1) for copper, nickel, lithium and cobalt under the Net Zero and Economic Transition Scenarios, with lithium at 3.5x in the ETS.
vol_and_positioning: Copper inventories are elevated in the US (COMEX) and low in China, reflecting tariff-front-running inflows.
Global gold ETF holdings are at a record 4,256 tonnes.
geopolitical: Kazatomprom shareholders withheld approval for a supply arrangement with Russia's Uranium One.
The Iran war is driving up energy costs and US inflation, per the footnote source.
China signalled it will keep rare earth and magnet export licensing flowing to the EU.
Tariff-driven trade distortions have pushed copper into US stockpiles and left China's low.

tension_points.bull_case: Chile output at its lowest since 2011, a four-year high in a Chinese import demand gauge and low Chinese stockpiles point to tightness outside the US.
tension_points.bear_case: A limited resumption at Cobre Panamá could add supply, and elevated US inventories show metal is available in the US.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A significant return of output at Cobre Panamá.

tension_points.bull_case: Record ETF inflows, 23 months of PBoC buying and record Chinese imports sustain bullion demand.
tension_points.bear_case: Stronger US consumer prices spurred bets on more aggressive Federal Reserve tightening, the dominant short-term driver.
